inputs.text: They’re framing this as routine border and immigration policy, but the timing is the tell: the measures follow Bill C-12 receiving royal assent on March 26, 2026. Calling it the “Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act” makes expanded control sound reassuring, while the headline singles out Nigerians and others. That looks less like neutral administration and more like a coordinated push to normalize tighter restrictions under the cover of security.
